content:
Let \(N\) be a 10-digit number, so \(10^9 \le N < 10^{10}\). Then
\[
10^{18} \le N^2 < 10^{20},
\]
so \(N^2\) has either 19 or 20 digits.

If \(N^2\) has 20 digits, then the first 10 digits of \(N^2\) are \(N\) exactly when
\[
N \le \frac{N^2}{10^{10}} < N+1.
\]
The left inequality gives \(N \ge 10^{10}\), impossible since \(N<10^{10}\). So no solutions here.

If \(N^2\) has 19 digits, then we need
\[
N \le \frac{N^2}{10^9} < N+1.
\]
The left inequality is automatic since \(N\ge 10^9\). The right inequality gives
\[
N^2 < (N+1)10^9.
\]
Write \(N=10^9+a\), where \(0\le a<9\cdot 10^9\). Then
\[
(10^9+a)^2 < (10^9+a+1)10^9.
\]
Expanding and simplifying:
\[
a(10^9+a) < 10^9.
\]
For integer \(a\ge 1\), the left side is at least \(10^9+1\), impossible. Thus \(a=0\).

Therefore the only solution is
\[
\boxed{1000000000}.
\]
